releases.name: v0.63.1: Signed Thinking Again
releases.body:
### Fixed

- **A thinking block keeps its signature on OpenCode 2.1.** The host renamed the reasoning event's payload field from `state` to `native` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts` publishes `native`; `packages/schema/session-legacy.ts` renames it on the durable events). Plugboard read `state` only, so on 2.1 every thinking block reached the caller with `signature: ""` while the reasoning text still arrived, and a client that sent that block back got it refused. The reasoning end now reads either field.

  Found by the check matrix on a hub running 2.1.4: `api: thinking/count_tokens` went from `thinking block signed` on 2.0.32 to `thinking block missing` on 2.1.4, reproducible on three runs.

## The full story

1 commit since v0.63.0, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Fixes (1)</summary>

**fix(session): read the reasoning signature from native on OpenCode 2.1** ([`e723e8e`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/e723e8e53b9ada5a55b3f3615956b681fcce2978))

OpenCode 2.1 renamed the reasoning event's payload field from `state` to `native`, so on 2.1.4 every thinking block reached the caller with an empty signature while its text still arrived.

Host evidence, both at the tags in anomalyco/opencode:

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts` publishes `native: native(event.providerMetadata)` on `session.reasoning.ended` (v2.1.4); v2.0.32 published the same value as `state`.
- `packages/schema/session-legacy.ts` carries the rename for durable events (`"session.reasoning.ended": ["state", "native"]`), and `SessionMessage.Native` is documented there as provider-owned replay data keyed by the producing provider's metadata fields, so the value is the same shape `signatureOf` already reads.

Found on the hub after the 2.1.4 upgrade: the check matrix row `api: thinking/count_tokens` reported `thinking block signed` on 2.0.32 and `thinking block missing` on 2.1.4, three runs in a row. The body of the /v1/messages answer carried the thinking text with `"signature": ""`, so the loss was in the plugin, not the provider.

`signatureOf` handled both the unwrapped and the provider-wrapped form, but the caller only ever passed `item.state`. The reasoning end now passes `item.state ?? item.native`, which keeps 2.0.x working (no `native` there) and restores the signature on 2.1.

Two tests in test/session/collector.test.ts cover the new field (a signature and a redacted block). Both fail with `state` only; with the fix the collector suite is 99 pass and the full suite 3875 pass, 130 skip, 0 fail. The test helper takes the field name as an argument so the old field stays a case of its own.

A client that replays an unsigned thinking block is refused, so this would have broken every Anthropic thinking conversation at its second turn on 2.1.

</details>

---

**Full diff:** [v0.63.0...v0.63.1](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/compare/v0.63.0...v0.63.1)

releases.name: v0.63.0: Runs on OpenCode 2.1
releases.body:
### Changed

- **OpenCode 2.1 is supported.** The `@opencode/plugin` peer range moves from `>=2.0.26 <2.1` to `>=2.0.26 <2.2`. Until now a 2.1.x server refused to load plugboard, which also kept an autoupdating server on 2.0.32: the host checks its peer range before it moves. Nothing in the plugin API moved. `dist/promise/index.d.ts`, `dist/effect/index.d.ts` and `dist/tui/index.d.ts` are byte-identical between `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.32 and 2.1.4, so `Plugin.define`, the plugin context and the TUI context are the same surface. 2.1 adds `ctx.session.list` and an optional `native` field on the prompt input, and neither is used here. The TUI half keeps its `@opentui` floor at 0.5.17: the host hands its own OpenTUI to a plugin at runtime, and 0.5.17 is what a 2.0.x host serves.

  Checked live on an isolated OpenCode 2.1.4 server. The plugin reports `state: active` with the `server`, `tui` and `rpc` features, `/v1/models` lists 478 models, a chat request creates its session and reaches the provider (the isolated home has no valid sign-in, so the provider refused it, which is upstream of plugboard), and the `/plugboard` page renders its tables and answers `w` with the 7 day range.

- **The devDependencies move to the new host**: `@opencode/plugin` 2.1.4 with `effect` 4.0.1. `npm-shrinkwrap.json` is regenerated as `check-pack` requires, which also takes `@opentelemetry/api` from 1.9.1 to 1.10.0, a transitive of `pino`. No direct runtime dependency changed.

## The full story

2 commits since v0.62.1, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Docs (1)</summary>

**docs: state the 2.1 support, the new pin and the peer range** ([`b1b599d`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/b1b599dc935404fd7250bdb26c2dc06dbfd859eb))

The supported-version line, the dev pin and the peer range in docs/architecture.md, docs/development.md, docs/packaging.md and AGENTS.md named 2.0.26 to 2.0.32 and `>=2.0.26 <2.1`. They now name the range the code declares.

architecture.md also said `ctx.session` has no `list`. That was true of 2.0.x and is not true of 2.1, so the sentence says which host gained it and why the index stays: the floor is still 2.0.26, and a host without `list` cannot answer the question the index answers.

packaging.md's host check now names `@opencode/plugin` 2.1.4 and the modules read at that version (`dist/host.js`, `dist/source.bun.js`, `dist/source.node.js`, `dist/runtime*.js`), all byte-identical to 2.0.32, which is the evidence the peer claim rests on.

Validation: `bun run docs:build`, `bun run lint` and `bun run format` pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Dependencies (1)</summary>

**build(deps): support opencode 2.1.4** ([`e911ea0`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/e911ea085e7ac140e67cbd024851c94d76ac6765))

OpenCode 2.1 shipped. Bumping the host pin moves the peer range's upper bound to `<2.2`, so an install on 2.1.x stops being refused, and the typecheck and the tests run against the new surface.

What changed in the host's plugin API, read from the two published packages rather than the release notes (`npm pack @opencode/plugin@2.0.32` and `@2.1.4`, then a file-by-file diff of `dist/`):

- The entry points are byte-identical: `dist/promise/index.d.ts`, `dist/effect/index.d.ts` and `dist/tui/index.d.ts` do not differ, so `Plugin.define`, the plugin context (`ctx.options`, `ctx.event`, `ctx.agent`, `ctx.tool`, `ctx.rpc`, `ctx.storage`, `ctx.location`, `ctx.app`), the TUI plugin context and every surface plugboard uses are unchanged.
- `SessionDomain` gains `list` (`dist/promise/session.d.ts`), and the adapter serves `session.list`. Additive: nothing plugboard calls moved or disappeared.
- The prompt input gains an optional `native` field, and `Permission.AssertInput.sessionID`'s brand loses a `descending` helper (internal to the host's ID factory). Neither is reachable from plugboard: it never sends `native`, and it passes a sess

releases.name: v0.62.1: Clearer Waiting Messages
releases.body:
### Changed

- **Two first-run messages say more.** `GET /readyz` and `GET /plugboard/ready` now explain the 503 you get after an OpenCode restart: "waiting for OpenCode to load plugboard", that the first model request to an app or a warm-up call makes it ready, and a link to the warm-up page. Readiness itself is unchanged: `/readyz` stays 503 until an app directory has served a request, because answering 200 earlier would send traffic to a server whose first request still has to boot the directory. An unknown model on a Gemini `generateContent`, `streamGenerateContent` or `countTokens` call now points at `GET /v1beta/models`, not `GET /v1/models`.

## The full story

1 commit since v0.62.0, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Fixes (1)</summary>

**fix(http): say why /readyz is 503 after a restart, and point Gemini at /v1beta/models** ([`0c21cdf`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/0c21cdf80d46eb3ed8f08ce88754f4bca5ebea1a))

Two bits of first-run friction left over from the last walkthrough.

/readyz: after an OpenCode restart it answered 503 "no app directory has been used since start; one model request to an app confirms it". The reason now starts with "waiting for OpenCode to load plugboard", says the first model request to an app or a warm-up call makes it ready, and links the warm-up page. The old phrase is still inside the text.

Gemini: an unknown model on generateContent, streamGenerateContent and countTokens said "GET /v1/models lists the models you can call", a route a Gemini client does not use. encodeGeminiError now rewrites that hint to GET /v1beta/models for model_not_found, so every path that reaches a Gemini error body (route, session, fallback) gets it. The GET /v1beta/models/{model} route already did.

Decision: readiness rule unchanged. servingConfirmed is the only signal that an app directory has booted in this process; answering 200 on listener-up alone would send load-balancer traffic to a server whose first request still boots the directory (a few seconds, and the pump and catalog load there too). Wording only.

Rejected: threading a list-route parameter through resolveModel, checkAppModel and the session caller. The encoder is the one place every Gemini error passes through.

Docs: errors.md (not_ready), configuration.md (errors table, /readyz line), warm-up.md. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Changed. Scripted transcripts of the four Gemini examples regenerated; each diff is only the message line (and its fieldViolations copy). Tests: newcomer-errors (generate, stream and count on a Gemini route), readyz (exact reason).

Validation: bun run validate --skip examples passes. The full examples step passed through every client up to langchain4j, which needs a Java runtime this machine lacks (unchanged OpenAI-shape transcripts).

</details>

---

**Full diff:** [v0.62.0...v0.62.1](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/compare/v0.62.0...v0.62.1)

releases.name: v0.62.0: Friendlier First Steps
releases.body:
### Changed

- **First-run messages say what to do next.** A wrong or missing key says to use a key from `keys`, not a provider key. An unknown model says that `GET /v1/models` (Gemini: `GET /v1beta/models`) lists the models you can call, and the 403 for an empty `models` shows `"models": "all"`. A `GET` on a `POST` route says which method it takes. A provider that rejected its sign-in says to run `/connect` on the OpenCode server and that your plugboard key is fine. An option name from before the renames (`history`, `maxN`, `cache`, `apps.<name>.models` and the rest) now fails at load with `it is renamed to <new name>`, `models: "connected"` says it is renamed to `"all"`, and a typo says `did you mean <name>?` instead of listing every option. The status codes, error codes and each API's error shape are unchanged.
- **`init` prints numbered next steps.** Restart OpenCode and touch the server (again after every restart), list the models, call one, and a link to the table of what to check when nothing answers. The key line no longer says "shown once" next to "it is also in the file".
- **The setup page reads cleanly and tells a browser user what to do.** Backtick spans in its hints and endpoint list show as code instead of literal backticks. Without a key, the page says a browser cannot send one and gives the curl that shows your models.
- **The install docs match what `init` does.** Every `init` command is `bunx opencode-plugboard@latest init`, so Bun cannot reuse an older copy and pin an old release. The first request lists the models first and sets `PLUGBOARD_KEY_MY_APP` from the printed key (the page called `fast`, which only exists with `--fast`). The "If it does not answer" table has the `provider_auth_failed` and invalid-options cases.

### Added

- **Split one app's usage by a request tag.** Send `x-plugboard-tag: cron` on any model request (Chat Completions, completions, Responses, Messages or Gemini) and the usage report counts requests, errors, tokens and cost per tag, next to the per-user split. `GET /plugboard/usage` has a `tags` object per app and a `?tag=` filter, and the dashboard Usage tab shows a Tags table. A tag is 1 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`; a bad one is ignored with a debug log line, never an error. A day keeps 100 tags per app and the rest count under `_other`. Prometheus metrics get no tag label, because a free-form value has unbounded cardinality. The CORS preflight allows the new header.
- **Ready-made monitoring for the Prometheus metrics.** `monitoring/prometheus-rules.yml` has recording rules and alerts for a high 5xx share, 429 refusals from limits and budgets, an open circuit breaker, fallback spikes, high p95 latency, a dead event pump and a missing or down scrape target. `monitoring/grafana-dashboard.json` imports into Grafana 11 with a datasource and an app variable: requests, errors, latency, tokens, cache hit ratio, breaker state, fallbacks and refusals. CI checks the rules with a pinned promtool, and a test keeps every metric and label they use in step with the exposition. Setup is in the monitoring guide. Cost and per-model figures are not metrics, so they stay in the usage report.
- **Control the response cache per request.** Send `x-plugboard-cache: bypass` to skip the cache for one call (no lookup, nothing stored), or `refresh` to skip the lookup and replace the stored answer. `x-plugboard-cache-namespace: <name>` keeps a caller's entries apart inside one app, and never reaches another app's entries. `Cache-Control: no-store` and `no-cache` mean `bypass` and `refresh`, and Portkey's namespace and force-refresh headers and Helicone's cache seed work too. The answer reports `bypass` or `refresh` in `x-plugboard-cache`. The headers only act for an app that uses `responseCache`; a bad value is a 400 `invalid_cache_header` in each API's own error shape. Browsers may send them: the CORS preflight now allows them.
- **Budgets: two windows on one metric are tested and documented.

releases.name: v0.61.0: Names All the Way
releases.body:
### Changed

- **Breaking: log events, metrics, a header and error codes follow the new option names.** The options were renamed in the last release, but the names you see at runtime still used the old words. They now match: the circuit breaker, OpenCode tools and sessions. There are no aliases, so update dashboards, alerts, log filters and error handling that use the old names:

  | Old | New |
  | --- | --- |
  | `plugboard_fallback_cooldown_events_total`, `plugboard_fallback_cooldown_targets` | `plugboard_circuit_breaker_events_total`, `plugboard_circuit_breaker_targets` |
  | `plugboard_history_sweeps_total`, `plugboard_history_sessions_removed_total` | `plugboard_sessions_sweeps_total`, `plugboard_sessions_removed_total` |
  | log events `fallback.cooldown.open`, `.skip`, `.close`, `.all_open` | `circuit_breaker.open`, `.skip`, `.close`, `.all_open` |
  | log events `history.swept`, `.sweep_failed`, `.sweep_timeout`, `.index_failed`, `.index_skipped` | `sessions.swept`, `.sweep_failed`, `.sweep_timeout`, `.index_failed`, `.index_skipped` |
  | log events `server_tool.call`, `server_tool.after_request` | `opencode_tool.call`, `opencode_tool.after_request` |
  | header `x-plugboard-server-tools` | `x-plugboard-opencode-tools` |
  | error codes `server_tool_collision`, `server_tool_denied_by_operator`, `server_tool_unavailable`, `server_tool_steps_exceeded`, `server_tool_calls_exceeded` | `opencode_tool_collision`, `opencode_tool_denied_by_operator`, `opencode_tool_unavailable`, `opencode_tool_steps_exceeded`, `opencode_tool_calls_exceeded` |
  | error code `app_has_server_tools` (admin keys) | `app_has_opencode_tools` |

  The `x-plugboard-opencode-tools` header is still in the CORS expose list. Internal names changed to match (for example `sweepSessions`, `sessionUrlTemplate`, `reportOpencodeTools`).

### Docs

- **A plainer home page.** The docs home opens with a short serif headline, one copyable install command (`bunx opencode-plugboard init`) and a terminal window that shows the first run and a curl call, instead of buttons and feature cards. The terminal is short (one curl line and a three line answer), so the sidebar and the first heading are visible on the first screen at 1440 by 900. The top bar is just the name, search, the latest release, the theme switch and GitHub. The pages that used to be in the top bar (guides, clients, reference, community) are in the sidebar. The headline font is installed from npm, so the site makes no font request to a third party.

## The full story

2 commits since v0.60.0, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Refactors (1)</summary>

**refactor(config): rename runtime names to match the renamed options** ([`2ec89f7`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/2ec89f7acb13966ed82210169f59f8fc52d44dd6))

The options were renamed in the last release (fallbackCooldown -> circuitBreaker, serverTools -> opencodeTools, history -> sessions), but the names an operator sees at runtime still used the old words. They now match. Breaking, accepted pre-1.0, no aliases.

What:
- Metrics: plugboard_fallback_cooldown_* -> plugboard_circuit_breaker_*; plugboard_history_sweeps_total / _sessions_removed_total -> plugboard_sessions_sweeps_total / plugboard_sessions_removed_total.
- Log events: fallback.cooldown.* -> circuit_breaker.*; history.swept, .sweep_failed, .sweep_timeout, .index_failed, .index_skipped -> sessions.*; server_tool.call / .after_request -> opencode_tool.*.
- Header x-plugboard-server-tools -> x-plugboard-opencode-tools, still in the CORS expose list.
- Error codes server_tool_* -> opencode_tool_*, app_has_server_tools -> app_has_opencode_tools.
- Internal names follow: sweepSessions, SessionLimits, appSessionLimits, sessionUrlTemplate, onHostedToolsFor, reportOpencodeTools, onOpencodeTools, ungrantedOpencodeTool, the events collector's opencodeCalls, the metrics sink's breaker(). Test files fallback-cooldown.tes
